title: The Red Planet Has Blue Sunsets. Here's Why

scenes.text: On Mars, the sunset is blue.
In April twenty fifteen, NASA's Curiosity rover filmed the Sun going down over Gale Crater.
The sky around the Sun glowed cool blue, while the rest of it turned a dusty orange. The exact opposite of Earth.
Here, air molecules scatter blue light away, so a sunset leaves only reds and oranges behind.
On Mars, the air is full of fine dust. That dust lets blue light pass straight through and keeps it close to the Sun.
So the red planet has blue sunsets, and the blue planet has red ones. Which one would you rather watch?

description:
On Mars, the sunset is blue. In April 2015, NASA's Curiosity rover filmed the Sun setting over Gale Crater, with a cool blue glow around the Sun and a dusty orange sky.
On Earth, air molecules scatter blue light away and leave reds behind. On Mars, fine dust lets blue light pass through and keeps it close to the Sun.
The red planet has blue sunsets, and the blue planet has red ones.
Which sunset would you rather watch?
